title: Office Madness
tagline: Pencils, a printer and a stapler against waves of very angry co-workers.
team: Team of 4, Level Up Lab 2.0 Team B
summary: Office Madness is a first-person wave shooter set in an open-plan office. Armed only with office supplies, you hold out against waves of furious colleagues while a minimap tracks who's coming for you. I built it over ten weeks with Level Up Lab 2.0, the student game dev team at Politecnico di Torino.
contribution: A first-person controller built on a state chart: walk, sprint, crouch, slide and jump, with head bob, camera roll, a landing kick and per-weapon screen shake.

Three office-supply weapons driven by their own state chart (idle, firing, empty): pencils thrown as projectiles that stick where they land, a printer that launches projectiles and a hitscan stapler, plus ammo, a three-slot inventory and pickups.

Three enemy types on a shared base class with NavigationAgent3D pathfinding: a rusher that punches, a shooter with hitscan spread and a thrower that fires on animation keys, all with a fresnel hit-flash shader.
A wave manager with a spawn queue, timers and spawn points, wired to the wave and enemies-left UI and the victory screen.
Minimap and full-screen map, pause and settings menus with key rebinding, gamepad support and the intro cutscene.
challenge: Keeping three very different weapons and a full movement set under control. I modelled both the player and the weapons as state charts, so every state and transition is explicit and visible in the debugger, and moved weapon stats (damage, range, hitscan or projectile) into Godot Resources: adding a weapon means a data file and a model, not new code.
credits: Made with Level Up Lab 2.0, Team B (Politecnico di Torino).

title: Life of Kengah
tagline: A hungry seagull, a bottomless ocean and one question: how deep is too deep?
role: TODO: your role, e.g. Gameplay programmer
summary: Built in two weeks for the FAIL/SAFE Jam 2025, Life of Kengah puts you in the wings of a seagull diving for fish. The deeper you go, the rarer and more valuable the catch, but your oxygen keeps dropping and nothing is safe until you're back on the boat.
contribution: Depth-based scoring that scales fish value with how far down you dive, pushing players toward the dark zone of the map.
An oxygen system that doubles as the run timer, wired to UI warnings that ramp up the tension as the bar empties.
State-based gameplay handling diving, catching and banking your haul at the boat, so a run's score only persists if you surface in time.
Collaborative pipeline to integrate art and sound with gameplay code inside the 14-day deadline.
challenge: Making risk feel fair: score, depth and oxygen had to be tuned together so that every dive is a readable decision instead of a coin flip, with a state machine that cleanly separates fish you're carrying from fish you've banked.
credits: Lorenzo Cattolico, Marco Silvestri, Francesco Perino, Nicolò Rizzo

title: Super Mario Music
tagline: A 3D platformer where you jump on the beat.
duration: TODO: how long it took, e.g. 2 months
team: Team of 4, Level Up Lab (Politecnico di Torino)
summary: A fan prototype made with Level Up Lab, the student game dev team at Politecnico di Torino. It mixes 3D movement inspired by Super Mario Odyssey and 3D World with rhythm-game timing: platforms move on the beat and a musical mushroom slows time down for the trickiest sections.
contribution: The 3D character controller and its physics, from the first prototype to the final movement feel.
The system that keeps moving platforms and level elements in sync with the music tracks.
Power-up logic, including the Musical Note Mushroom and its time-dilation effect.
challenge: Keeping gameplay locked to the soundtrack: platforms are driven by the music's timing rather than by frame time, and slowing the world down with the power-up had to keep the rhythm readable for the player.
credits: Programming by Lorenzo Cattolico; music, art direction and coordination by three teammates at Level Up Lab.
